Jamie Overton to Matt Renshaw, 1 run, Australia have won the first ODI and taken a 1-0 lead in the three-match series, chasing down the target with more than 24 overs to spare. A thoroughly dominant performance from the hosts, who have blown England away in the series opener. Swipes this towards deep mid-wicket. It doesn't have the legs to reach the boundary, but the batters have all the time in the world to complete the single and take Australia past England's total

But this game was all about debutant Mahli Beardman (6/24), who registered the best-ever bowling figures by an Australian on ODI debut. Beardman, Spencer Johnson and Xavier Bartlett did all the damage in the first innings, making the job incredibly easy for the batters.

Spencer Johnson (1/2): Yeah, obviously, one-day cricket in Australia. I feel like that's, as a kid, you grow up... I grew up watching it, and to be playing it is pretty special. [You took three wickets yourself, but how do you dissect a performance from a young guy (Mahli Beardman) in his first one-day game?] Mahli's not short on confidence. He's got lots of energy. He was made for this, so we're going to see him in green and gold a lot, I think. [What are you taking to Adelaide moving forward now?)] Obviously, I think this is our only one-day series we've got until the World Cup coming up. So it's quite an important one. There's some fresh faces here, and hopefully we can go 3-0.

Johnson (2/2): [And just on yourself, obviously missed a lot of cricket over the last sort of 18 months with a few injuries, got married in the off-season as well. But I guess being back out there, taking three wickets, what does that do for your confidence now? Not just for yourself, but in your body moving forward] Yeah, it's obviously nice to perform and contribute, but injuries, it's part of it, professional sport. So good to be back, and hopefully I can stay in the park from here on in.

Beardman 2/2: [On dealing with injuries and the doubts that came with his recovery] A little bit, I think. I think it's pretty natural, particularly after a stress-related injury in your back. You obviously got, six to eight months out. So there's always doubt. I don't think I've ever lost my love for the game. That's nothing that sort of seems to go away. I think it's more just will I come back and be able to bowl the same again, and will there be that speed there, and all those sort of questions. But yeah, as I said, it's such an amazing group, and just to be back in this space and with this team is such an honour.

Harry Brook | England captain (1/2): [Harry, tough day. I'll start with the bowling for Australia. How did you see it? Young man, he's going to be the headline act tomorrow, isn't he? What was the feedback from the batting group] Yeah. We've been here for a week and a half or so. We've prepared extremely well. Australia have bowled extremely well. Mahli Beardman was outstanding today. He put the ball in the right areas, got enough out of the surface to dismiss us, and, yeah, they put in a good performance with the ball. [On the team's batting performance] We spoke a lot about adaptability. We want to adapt to different surfaces, and like I said before, we've been here for a week and a half. We prepared extremely well. We knew that certain shots weren't going to work on this pitch, but look, the Australian attack bowled extremely well. They put the ball in the right areas for 30-odd overs, and we probably didn't execute our skill well enough.

Brook (2/2): [Still 11 months out from the World Cup. That's not a lot of time. So I guess that campaign really starts now, and you've got time to change things.] Definitely, and that is the bigger picture. We've got a World Cup in South Africa in 12 months' time, and these experiences, we take them, we learn from them as much as we possibly can. We're not out of this series yet. We've been in this position a couple of times before and managed to bounce back. So hopefully we can do that when we get to Adelaide.

Marsh (2/2): [On his knock] Yeah, 130 on paper always looks like a really easy chase. This wicket has its own characteristics, and it can be challenging. We sort of spoke about as a group that that first 20 overs is not similar to other one-days, where you sort of get off to a flyer and work your way into it. You really have to work hard for that first 20 overs here, and I love that characteristic about this ground. We play on so many flat, beautiful batting wickets around the world, and this place has got its own character within the crowd and stands and the wicket itself, and I love playing here. It's my home. But, yeah, it was a really good chase in the end.

International cricket must feel like a breeze for Mahli Beardman right now! The 21-year-old has blown away almost an entire batting line-up on debut, something you don't get to witness very often. But that's exactly what he managed to do against England today. And Australia continue to dominate this rivalry, having now won 11 of the last 14 ODIs between these two sides. They have drawn first blood in the series, but with two games still to go, England will be desperate to hit back. The second ODI takes us to Adelaide, where the conditions should be far more conducive to batting than what we witnessed here in Perth today.
